$comment: DRAFT ledger for issue #60: Martin Scorsese only. Same schema as essential10-example.json (schemaVersion 1); extra optional fields: films[].flags, nearMisses[].imdb/rt. Not approved, not for app use until the owner signs off the roster, the method and the score-display licensing decision.
methodSummary: Eligibility (sole or credited TMDB Directing credit, feature or, where flagged, feature-length documentary) -> longlist with evidence panel -> tier by directing achievement (craft, innovation, influence, canon) with IMDb and RT used only as within-source ordinal sanity checks -> order within tier by documented editorial judgement. IMDb /10 and Tomatometer % are never averaged or combined.

imdb.source: IMDb non-commercial dataset title.ratings.tsv.gz (ratings and vote counts); title.basics and title.crew used to match ids and confirm sole directors
imdb.note: Dataset file run-date 2026-11-12, last-modified 2026-11-13 00:28 GMT. The live IMDb title page returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool on 2026-11-13, so ratings were not cross-checked against live pages. Dataset licence is personal / non-commercial use only; see SCORE_SOURCING_NOTES.md.

rt.source: Rotten Tomatoes film page, critics Tomatometer percentage and its critic review count
rt.note: Read through a text-extraction fetch tool, one film page at a time. Percentages were cross-checked against the RT celebrity filmography table where it listed them and, for some films, against search-result summaries of the same page. Review counts are live and change daily; each is a single dated read.

films.title: GoodFellas
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: A gangster life told from inside, with voice-over, freeze-frames and the Copacabana tracking shot turned into a method of narration; the highest IMDb rating in his filmography and the most-cited example of his editing with Thelma Schoonmaker.

films.title: Taxi Driver
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: Palme d'Or winner that turns a city at night into a character's mental state; defining 1970s American film and the template for the alienated urban protagonist.

films.title: Raging Bull
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: Boxing biography staged as the self-destruction of a man and filmed in black and white with subjective, stylised fight sequences; regularly named among the best American films of the 1980s.

films.title: Mean Streets
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: The breakthrough film: a personal, hand-held, rock-scored view of small-time criminals and Catholic guilt that fixed his themes and style; strong Tomatometer but the lowest IMDb rating in the ten (7.1).

films.title: The Departed
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: A tightly plotted crime thriller adapted from a Hong Kong film, and the work that brought him the Best Director and Best Picture Oscars; very high on both evidence lines.

films.title: The King of Comedy
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).

rt.rtYearNote: RT lists 1983 (US release); TMDB and the original release are 1982. WARNING: RT /m/1099397-king_of_comedy is a different 2007 film.

films.rationale: A discomforting comedy of fame and obsession, misunderstood at release and now widely seen as prescient; a formal departure from his crime films.

films.title: Casino
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: Three-hour Las Vegas epic that pushes his GoodFellas methods (voice-over, montage, fast editing) toward operatic scale; high audience standing, mixed critic score, so kept below the films that score on both lines.

films.title: The Last Waltz
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB and IMDb). DOCUMENTARY / concert film, flagged per the owner's decision that documentaries may be included where essential.

rt.rtYearNote: RT URL carries a 1978 suffix. WARNING: RT /m/the_last_waltz is a different 1936 film.

films.rationale: Concert documentary of The Band's farewell show, shot by a team of leading cinematographers and treated as a feature with staged interviews; the closest thing in his work to a pure formal experiment in capturing performance.

films.title: After Hours
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).

rt.rtYearNote: WARNING: IMDb tt0086858 is an unrelated 1985 short with the same title; tt0088680 is Scorsese's film.

films.rationale: A nightmare-comedy of one night downtown, made at speed on a low budget after a failed project; a showcase of invention in framing and pacing and a favourite of critics.

films.title: Killers of the Flower Moon
films.directorCreditNote: Sole director (TMDB Directing credit; IMDb dataset lists the same sole director).
films.rationale: A late-career crime film about the murders of Osage people in 1920s Oklahoma, told with a slow, moral pace and a collaboration with editor Thelma Schoonmaker; the strongest recent film and the closest call (see below).

nearMisses.title: The Irishman
nearMisses.reason: Strong on both lines (IMDb 7.8, RT 95%) but largely restates his gangster themes and ranks just behind Killers of the Flower Moon on a different, newer subject; the first alternate.

nearMisses.title: The Age of Innocence
nearMisses.reason: Most refined period film; lower audience standing (7.2, 76,156 votes).

nearMisses.title: Shutter Island
nearMisses.reason: IMDb 8.2 but only 69% on the Tomatometer; a genre piece.

nearMisses.title: The Wolf of Wall Street
nearMisses.reason: IMDb 8.2, RT 79%; overlaps with GoodFellas and Casino in method.

nearMisses.title: Hugo
nearMisses.reason: 93% on RT but IMDb 7.5; a family film that sits outside his main body of work.

nearMisses.title: Silence
nearMisses.reason: Serious late work but RT 83% and IMDb 7.2.

unverified: TMDB film ids and Directing credits were read from the TMDB person page on 2026-11-13 (no TMDB API key was available), not from the API crew.job field; title-to-id pairs were taken from the page links. Co-director status was checked against the IMDb dataset crew file (title.crew), which lists a sole director for every film in the list.
IMDb ids were matched in the IMDb dataset by original title, year and runtime, not read from a TMDB external_ids field; confirm with the TMDB API external_ids at implementation.
RT review counts are a single read on the stated date via a text fetcher.
IMDb title pages could not be read (HTTP 403); ratings and votes come from the official dataset (not cross-checked against the live pages), whose licence is non-commercial only.
Shutter Island RT review count was 260 on the page read and 262 in a search-result snapshot the same day; 260 is recorded.

RT numbers for The King of Comedy, After Hours, The Age of Innocence, Casino, The Last Waltz and Shutter Island matched the percentage and count shown in search-result summaries as well as the film page; the Scorsese celebrity page on RT only showed recent titles, so the celebrity-table cross-check used for Kubrick, Miyazaki and Bong was not possible for most of Scorsese's list.
